summary: Bodies keep one identity through the features that change them. src/domain/cad/cadBodies.ts derives the bodies after each feature from the history and each kind's declared body behaviour. A body is keyed by the feature that created it, plus an occurrence where that feature makes a copy or a piece: inst(i,j) for a pattern copy, split(k) for a piece of a split body and mirror for a mirror image. A feature that modifies a body (fillet, chamfer, shell, move, cut, join, pocket and the patterns) keeps its key and is recorded in modifiedBy. A Boolean keeps its target's key and records itself as consumedBy on each tool. Each state is { key, kind, createdBy, modifiedBy, consumedBy?, pieces?, ambiguous?, untracked? }. Validation and the kernel resolve a stored target through this lineage, strictly by the feature whose result the body now is, as before, so every diagnostic is unchanged. The kernel keys its bodies by body key and tracks the parts of a body, its split pieces and separate pattern copies, only where continuity is certain. Each solid of a feature's result is traced to every source solid it keeps a face of unchanged: the target's pieces, each pattern copy and a fused tool. A solid that continues one target piece keeps its key, a copy is inst(i,j) of the piece copied, and a piece split again is split(q), numbered by the first face it keeps, never by position, size or centroid. Anything else gets a fresh feature/split(k) key, a reported ambiguity or a reported loss, never a guess, and ambiguity carries to every descendant. CadBuildResult.bodyIssues reports each feature's ambiguous-body-parts, lost-body-parts and untracked-body-parts, with more-body-issues past 512: a hook D1 can adopt. Every build returns the body states (CadBuildResult.bodies, CadMesh.bodyKey), and the worker reply check verifies them against the meshes. Consumers choose bodies by key: a command started with a feature selected (Fillet, Chamfer, Move, the patterns, Mirror, Pocket and the target of a Boolean) and File > Section for CAM now act on the body that feature leads to, wherever it sits in that body's history, instead of falling back to the latest body. The DXF export dialog's initial body is chosen the same way, and cad_build rows add bodyKey. Stored targets still hold feature ids and nothing stored changes. S8's CadBodyRef and CadBodyMetadata shapes and their resolution are defined and tested but not stored. docs/maintainers/cad-features.md describes body identity.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. The CAD document and edit schemas, agent tool schemas and descriptions, parsed documents, diagnostics, kernel geometry, sections, STL exports and saved bytes in the browser cache and folder adapters are identical to main at 5ab4b5ea (0.0.795), this change's base. Two additive changes are visible. cad_build body rows gain a bodyKey field beside featureId, which agents may ignore; tools still take featureId as bodyId. With a feature selected that is no longer the latest state of its body, such as a pad that was later filleted, starting Fillet, Chamfer, Move, a pattern, Mirror, Pocket or a Boolean, or opening File > Section for CAM, now targets that pad's body in its filleted state instead of the most recently changed body.

checklist.schema: No CAD document, sketch, UPID, post, machine package, saved revision, storage or journal change. The published CAD document schema, edit schema and every feature variant are byte-identical. Body keys are derived on every rebuild and never stored; stored target, source and tool fields still hold feature ids. The worker build reply gains optional bodies, bodyIssues and CadMesh.bodyKey fields. The main thread and the worker ship together, and the reply check accepts a reply without them, as older build results are. When present, it requires one body state per mesh, in mesh order, whose key is the mesh's bodyKey, whose current feature is the mesh's featureId and whose pieces, when present, key the mesh's solids one for one; it requires unique mesh keys and at most 512 issues. A list of part keys holds at most 4,096 keys, and an issue message gives counts, never part keys. A body with more parts, or a longer part key, is reported as untracked, so a large valid model is summarised, never refused. Post engine API remains 1, saved-job engine remains 3 and CAD_PRECISION_VERSION stays 2. S8's CadBodyRef and CadBodyMetadata are types and resolution functions only.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation, input-version or WebMCP guard change. Initial CAD discovery stays at 51,178 of its 51,200 UTF-8 bytes: no tool name, description or input schema changes. cad_describe_features and cad_describe_edits return byte-identical replies. cad_build body rows add bodyKey, the creating feature id with any occurrence (such as flip/mirror), after featureId; docs/site/agents.md explains it. Every diagnostic code and message is unchanged. The only new codes, ambiguous-body-parts, lost-body-parts, untracked-body-parts and more-body-issues, are body issues returned in bodyIssues, never diagnostics.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change and no new application controls. Commands started with a feature selected now choose that feature's body by key; with no selection, or a selection that leads to no drawn body, they choose the latest body as before. The Boolean tool default is the latest other body, as before.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change. Kernel geometry, mesh order, previews, sections and STL exports are byte-identical. STEP export writes the same bodies in the same order under the same names, the feature names, until S8 stores body metadata.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Every parity document loads, validates, rebuilds and saves to identical bytes through both the browser cache and folder adapters.
checklist.verification: Parity, against main at 5ab4b5ea (0.0.795), the base of this change, captured on the base tree and on this one: agent tool metadata (51,178 bytes), the cad_describe_features and cad_describe_edits replies, the document and edit schemas are byte-identical. So are, over 86 documents (the 17 kernel parity models, the 6 benchmark steps, 41 sketch fixture parts and 22 body histories of modifying features, Booleans, nested patterns, mirrors, splits and suppression), parsed documents, validation, feature inputs and dependencies, parameter inspection and the bytes each document saves, loads and saves again through the browser cache and folder adapters (172 saves). So are the codes and messages of 3,578 diagnostics from mutated variants of them: suppression toggles, deletions, features moved first or last, every id field retargeted or cleared, changed operations and a Boolean tool pointed at its own target. Over the same 86 documents, every kernel build fingerprint, diagnostic, mesh (positions, indices, face and edge groups, with the random per-build topology keys numbered by first appearance), section, topology descriptor and STL export is identical; the kernel parity snapshot test passes unchanged. The kernel's body states equal the domain lineage for every kernel parity model, and each build reply passes the worker reply check. Identity tests: src/domain/cad/__tests__/cadBodies.test.ts (40 tests) covers keys and their text form, the lineage of every body behaviour, suppression, reorder and delete, the body parts each kind of kernel fact gives (piece ranks, solids keeping no face, merges, losses, the bridge and island, inherited ambiguity, pattern copies separate, merged, nested and vanished, limits and overflow, issue messages and the issue cap), the S8 reference and metadata resolution, selection by key and the checks of values received from the worker. src/features/cad/kernel/cadKernelBodies.test.ts (21 tests, in the kernel) covers keys through fillet, chamfer, shell, move, pocket, cut, join and Boolean, pattern copies and mirror keys, piece numbering by kept faces for three cut positions built twice each (the right piece is split(0) although the kernel lists it second), pieces through a move, a second split and a joined island, an ambiguous cleave, the five review round 1 repros, a reply whose pieces do not match its solids, and a property test over random histories. A workbench test checks that selecting a filleted pad sends Section for CAM and Move to the pad's body and not to a later block. Mutations, each alone against the identity suites, the kernel parity test and the workbench test, all 16 caught. The four from before review, rerun at head: a modifying feature minting its own key fails 33 tests (12 domain, 20 kernel, 1 workbench); a Boolean keeping its tool's key fails 4; selection falling back to the latest body by position fails 2; split pieces ordered by centroid fail 4 kernel tests. Twelve break the inheritance rule or the reply limits: a tool-only island taking a piece no solid continues (3), a solid keeping no face taking a piece left over by elimination (3), a merged solid keeping the first target key (4), ambiguity not inherited (4), losses not reported (8), unidentifiable pieces dropped instead of left ambiguous (2), pieces carried over whenever the solid count is unchanged (6), a whole body splitting only when the count grows (1), the ambiguity message listing every key (2), parts not capped at 4,096 (1), pattern copies' faces not recorded (4) and a join's tool faces not traced (2). The random-history property test alone catches seven of the twelve; it first missed the inherited-ambiguity mutation and now checks that every piece keeping or extending an ambiguous key stays ambiguous. Since review round 1. All five findings are fixed under one rule: a key is inherited only when continuity is certain; anything else gets a fresh key, a reported ambiguity or a reported loss, never a guess. createCadKernelFaceSources replaces cadKernelSolidOrigins and records the faces of every source a feature combines (the target's solids, each pattern copy before it is released, and a fused tool); cadBodyParts gives each result solid its key from the source solids it keeps faces of. occurrences is removed: pattern copies are traced per solid into pieces. ambiguous-split-order is replaced by ambiguous-body-parts, lost-body-parts, untracked-body-parts and more-body-issues. (1) A valid build failed the worker check because the ambiguity message listed every key (9,721 characters). Messages now give counts and keep the keys in pieces; lists hold at most 4,096 keys, past which a body is reported untracked; issues stop at 512 with a summary; modifiedBy stays uncapped and checked by entry; and the reply check requires pieces to key the mesh's solids one for one. 100 copies of a cleaved rod created by a 36-character UUID id give 200 ambiguous keys, a 123-character message and a reply that passes the check. (2) An island joined beside a split box inherited a piece's key by elimination. Every solid is now traced to every predecessor it keeps faces of: the island gets bridge/split(0), the bridged solid bridge/split(1), and both box pieces are reported lost and resolve as missing. (3) A pocket in one piece of a cleaved cylinder erased its ambiguity. Ambiguity now carries to every descendant, and the pieces stay ambiguous candidates. (4) A pattern copy cut away still resolved. Copies are traced per solid, so the cut reports box/inst(1,0) lost and it resolves as missing. (5) A cut that split one patterned cube and removed the other went unseen because the count did not change. Splits and losses are found per predecessor solid, never by totals; the repro gives box/inst(0,0)/split(0) and split(1) and reports box/inst(1,0) lost. Each repro is a kernel test, and a property test over random histories (10 seeds of 5 steps from a box or disc, drawing patterns, one- to three-slot splits, cuts, one- or two-profile joins and pockets) checks at every step that no key repeats, that each piece keeps or extends a key from before or is a fresh key of the step's feature, that a solid inheriting a key without ambiguity overlaps its predecessor, that ambiguity is reported and inherited, that no piece vanishes unreported, that every reported loss resolves as missing then and later, and that rebuilds are identical. The kernel gives kept faces cheaply but not faces a Boolean's simplification merges: an extruded circle's two half side faces are merged by a pattern's fuse, so the copies of round hole and boss patterns keep no face and get fresh, ambiguous keys instead of guessed ones until K3 provides the Boolean's own face history. Parity after round 1 is byte-identical in everything stored, diagnosed or built; derived body states or issues changed in 18 of the 86 documents, all as the rule requires. Timing, by minimums of back-to-back main and branch runs with the tree order alternating; an overlapping run is noted by the number of two-second samples in which another checkout ran a test, build, type check or benchmark. Rebuild (benchmark-cad, six pairs): build and shipped edit stay within about 3% either way on all three benchmark models: plate-hole-pattern build 61.68 to 62.50 ms and shipped edit 60.13 to 60.23 ms, gear-and-plate build 430.68 to 417.55 ms and shipped edit 421.84 to 433.60 ms, box-fillet-all-edges build 36.11 to 36.56 ms and shipped edit 34.84 to 35.41 ms. Pair 2 overlapped on main (50 samples), pair 3 on the branch (25) and pair 4 on both (6 and 25); pairs 5 and 6 were quiet, but the machine ran about twice as slowly for both trees. Worker reply check (isCadKernelReply on captured build replies, four pairs, two of them clean): replies now carry body states, so the check costs a little more, 1,911.5 to 1,958.3 µs for all 23 replies (2.4%) and 370 to 388 µs (4.9%) for the largest, the gear-and-plate rebuild reply, against a 420 ms build; cloning the reply is unchanged. Document load (parse and validation, 60 runs per measure, four pairs, two of them clean): 32 sketches 48.47 to 48.62 ms, 32 extruded sketches 102.60 to 104.96 ms (paired median ratio 1.006), 8 extruded sketches 24.29 to 23.25 ms and the 23 parity and benchmark documents 25.75 to 26.03 ms (paired median ratio 1.004); the benchmark-cad parse, drag preview and viewport reference measures are within noise. Pointer moves: hovering a plane renders the workbench again. Main recomputed the visible-body set on every render. This branch derives the lineage once per document, the drawn body ids once per build and the Section for CAM body once per selection, so pointer moves recompute no body list. Deriving the lineage of all 23 documents takes 0.08 ms against 0.02 ms for main's visible set, about 2.5 µs per document, once per document version. Bundle, production builds of main at 5ab4b5ea and this branch: the kernel worker grows from 770,415 to 775,634 bytes (+5,219, +2,472 gzipped) for the lineage, the piece origins and the reply checks. The shared CAD chunk with the feature definitions now also holds the lineage and is emitted as two preloaded chunks, cadFeatureInputs (49,809 bytes) and cadParameters (6,104 bytes), instead of one of 50,415 bytes: +5,498 bytes, +2,399 gzipped, and one more small request on first load. The worker client grows by 523 bytes and every other chunk by 3 to 156 bytes. All JavaScript and CSS grow by 11,777 bytes (0.19%), 5,336 gzipped (0.30%). Checks: the full Vitest run passes (629 files, 7,357 tests); npm run build passes, including the type check, the documentation check and the corresponding-source checks; npm run lint has zero findings; npm run ui:check passes; check-release passes on its own and fails against origin/main only because the previous version, 0.0.796, is still in review while main is at 0.0.795. Specs, each run alone with two workers against the production build while the end-to-end port was free: cad-workflow including Section for CAM and sending the section to CAM (32), cad-kernel (2), cad-topology-repick (3), cad-region-workflow (1), cad-intersecting-areas (1), cad-plane-selection-section (6) and project-navigation with saved CAD, reload and STEP export (2), 47 tests, all pass. cad-kernel, cad-region-workflow, cad-topology-repick and cad-workflow check cad_build body rows through the agent tools. No controller or machine verification is claimed; no output path changed.

publicNotes.summary: CAD bodies keep their identity through the features that change them.
changes: With a feature selected, Fillet, Chamfer, Move, the patterns, Mirror, Pocket, Boolean and Section for CAM act on the body that feature belongs to, even after later features changed it.
CAD build results for agents name each body by the feature that created it (bodyKey), which stays the same through later changes.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, CAD files and controller output are unchanged.
